claim: Women aren't interested in playing sports.

claim: Title IX was enacted in 1972 and bans sex discrimination in federally funded education programs.
notes: Historical fact.

claim: Girls' high school sports participation has grown over 1,000% since Title IX.
notes: NFHS: ~294K girls in 1971-72 to ~3.4M in 2018-19. Verify.

claim: The USWNT earned less than the USMNT in bonuses despite strong results.
notes: Rewritten to be specific. Pre-2022 CBA era. Verify wording.

claim: Female NCAA athlete numbers have hit record highs in recent years.
notes: Draft: 242,341 in 2024-25. Verify with NCAA.

claim: The share of women coaching NCAA women's teams has dropped since Title IX.
notes: Acosta/Carpenter: 90%+ in 1972 to ~40-43%. Verify.

claim: Women's sports leagues are profitable.
notes: Depends on league. Draft: WSL revenue up but big losses. Verify.

claim: Women's sports get equal prize money to men's.
notes: Relabeled 2026-10-03 from mixed: tennis majors are the exception, most sports are far from equal. Tennis Grand Slams equal. FIFA WWC 2023 pool $110M vs men's 2022 $440M (1/4, draft said 1/3). Verify.

claim: Female athletes are more injury-prone than male athletes.
notes: ACL tears more common in women. Other injuries not. Depends on type.

claim: Title IX achieved gender equality in college sports.
notes: Huge participation gains but gaps remain. Could argue busted. Decide.
